title: data-cap Evidence Model
description: Canonical, versioned composition of Capability/Dependency/Ownership/Finding/Change/Runtime Contract Model into one provenance-stamped artifact (see ADR 0050). Generated from src/build/evidence-model.ts's EvidenceModel type -- never hand-authored.

provenance.description: Who/when/what produced this instance -- always present (see `EvidenceProvenance`).

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle Model -- always populated, for the reason `EvidenceModelInputs.lifecycle` documents.

computed.description:
Which of the four optional sub-models below this run actually computed
-- read this before concluding anything from an absent one (OUT-04).

dependency.description: Dependency Model, or `undefined` when no usage scan was run -- see `computed.dependency` before reading absence as "no dependencies."

ownership.description: Ownership Model, or `undefined` when none was supplied -- see `computed.ownership`.

finding.description: Finding Model, or `undefined` when nothing was supplied -- see `computed.finding` before reading absence as "no findings."

change.description: Change Model, or `undefined` when no manifest diff was available -- see `computed.change` before reading absence as "nothing changed." Not a diffable input across two `EvidenceModel`s the way the other five project-varying fields conceptually are -- it already IS a diff.

runtimeContract.description: Runtime Contract Model -- always populated, package-scoped rather than project-scoped (see this module's own doc comment). A static append, never itself a diffable "changed since last run" input.

EvidenceModel.description: `data-cap`'s Evidence Model: the composition of Capability, Lifecycle, Dependency, Ownership, Finding, Change, and Runtime Contract Model into one provenance-stamped artifact.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp for when this evidence was generated.

toolVersion.description: `data-cap`'s own installed version at generation time.

commit.description: The commit SHA this evidence was generated against, or `undefined` when the caller didn't supply one.

EvidenceProvenance.description:
Who/when/what produced a given `EvidenceModel` instance -- matching env-cap's own `EvidenceProvenance` shape exactly, so a consumer reading both packages' evidence artifacts reads one vocabulary, not two.

`generatedAt`/`toolVersion` are required: every real caller can supply both (the tool version is `data-cap`'s own installed version, read from its `package.json` -- see `package-version.ts`), and a provenance stamp that might be missing either one is a provenance stamp no consumer can rely on. `commit` stays caller-supplied and explicitly `string | undefined` (never omitted from the shape): `data-cap` never shells out to `git` itself, so an absent commit is a stated absence, never a guess -- ADR 0050's "provenance is caller-supplied, never ambient-detected" convention, kept exactly where it still applies.

warnings.description: Parse/link warnings carried through from the discovery/linking pass that produced this inventory, each `file` root-relative like every other path this model publishes (OUT-01).

CapabilityInventory.description: The one authoritative model every report generator reads from -- see `buildInventory`. This type IS `data-cap`'s Capability Model (ADR 0050), not a separate thing that produces one: `CAPABILITY_MODEL_SCHEMA_VERSION` above versions this exact interface. ADR 0050 deliberately kept the `CapabilityInventory`/`buildInventory` names rather than introducing a `CapabilityModel`/`buildCapabilityModel` wrapper, since this type was already the intended public model before that ADR existed -- a rename would duplicate an already-correct, already-public shape for no gain. A canonical, versioned, JSON-serializable projection of every discovered capability's fields and operations, active or not.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring this capability -- the one place an absolute discovery path is converted for publication (OUT-01, see `display-path.ts`). Every downstream model that carries a capability's `file` (Ownership, Finding, Dependency, Manifest Snapshot) copies this value rather than re-deriving it, so there is exactly one conversion point. Re-derive a real path with `absolutePathFrom(root, file)` when actual filesystem/import work needs one.

exportName.description: The binding name the `buildData`/`createData` result is exported as.

kind.description: `"buildData"` or `"createData"` -- which call form declared this capability.

docs.description: This capability's own declared documentation, if any -- the single path for `owner`/`sensitivity`/`purpose`/`legalBasis`/`dataResidency`/`auditRequired` (ADR 0057): a capability has nothing above it to resolve against, so a separate top-level "resolved" property would only ever duplicate `docs.X` verbatim.

declarationPosition.description: Position of this capability's own `buildData`/`createData` call site -- always available (ADR 0052).

CapabilityNode.description: One `buildData`/`createData` capability, resolved from the inventory's shared model.

name.description: Display name -- falls back to the export/binding name when omitted.

description.description: Why this capability exists / what it's for.

owner.description: Who's accountable for this capability. A field's own `owner` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically.

exclusiveGroup.description: Mutual-exclusivity group: more than one *active* capability sharing this value is a real conflict (only one implementation of a group should be live at once).

active.description: Defaults to `true` when omitted. Gates `exclusiveGroup` conflict checks and manifest membership.

sensitivity.description: Data classification. Standard vocabulary: `"public"` / `"internal"` / `"confidential"` / `"restricted"` (ascending) -- custom values are allowed but flagged as non-standard, never blocking.

protections.description: Documented safeguard -- presence only, never an adequacy claim.

retention.description: Documented retention policy -- presence only, never an enforcement claim.

purpose.description: The declared reason this capability's data is collected/retained. Declared only -- data-cap never verifies the stated purpose matches actual usage. A field's own `purpose` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically.

legalBasis.description: The declared legal basis asserted for processing this capability's data (e.g. `"consent"`, `"contract"`, `"legitimate interest"`). Records that a basis was declared -- never that data-cap has determined the basis is legally valid; data-cap records declared governance facts, it does not determine whether those facts satisfy a law. A field's own `legalBasis` overrides this for that field specifically.

dataResidency.description: The declared jurisdiction(s) this capability's data is permitted/ expected to be *stored* in -- a policy constraint, not an observed fact, not a processing-location claim, not a data-subject-location claim. A field's own `dataResidency` overrides this for that field specifically.

auditRequired.description: Whether access to this capability's data is documented as requiring an audit trail. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as `protections`/`retention`. A field's own `auditRequired` overrides this for that field specifically.

expiresAt.description: When this capability's data (or the credential/source behind it) is declared to stop being valid, as an ISO-8601 date. A field's own `expiresAt` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically. Declared only -- nothing expires at runtime.

deprecated.description: Whether this capability is documented as deprecated. Presence-only; nothing warns at runtime.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this capability is deprecated, and what to use instead. Only meaningful alongside `deprecated`.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for -- opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package (e.g. jurisdiction-specific regulatory classification: `{ regulatory: "GDPR,PCI-DSS" }`). Once a concept matters enough for data-cap to reason about, it gets its own named field above (as `purpose`/`legalBasis`/`dataResidency`/`auditRequired` did); everything else stays here.

evidence.description: Developer-supplied evidence assertions -- verified over time, unlike every other field above, which is declared-only. Kept structurally separate for exactly that reason (see `EvidenceFieldDocs`).

LooseCapabilityDocs.description: `CapabilityDocs` is parameterized by the real `documentData()` schema type so authored calls get `keyof`-checked field/getter/mutator/subscription names -- but this module (and `inventory.ts`/`link.ts`, which reuse this exact type) deals only in already-parsed AST facts, with no compile-time schema of its own to check against. `LooseCapabilityDocs` is the build- tool-internal equivalent of "structurally shaped like docs, unconstrained" the old bare `Record<string, unknown>` parameter gave: every OTHER property comes from `CapabilityDocs` itself (via `Omit`), but `fields`/`getters`/`mutators`/`subscriptions` are redeclared as plain `Record<string, X>` maps rather than routed through `CapabilityDocs`' own `keyof`-checked generics -- `DataSchema`'s `getters`/etc. are themselves optional properties, which resolve to "no keys allowed" (not "any key allowed") once `CapabilityDocs` requires a concrete schema type, exactly backwards from what an unconstrained AST-parsed fact needs here.

dynamicAccess.description: Citations of where this field is accessed in a way static analysis can't see on its own (e.g. a truly dynamic key derived at runtime), each `"<relative-path>:<line>:<column>"`. Re-verified every run: a citation whose file no longer exists, or whose cited line has visibly changed since the citation was written, is downgraded and flagged, never trusted forever.

EvidenceFieldDocs.description: Developer-supplied evidence assertions for one field -- categorically different from every field on `FieldDocs`: those are declared-and-never- verified (ADR 0049's own invariant), while `dynamicAccess` is re-checked against reality every run (see the build-tooling side of this feature). Kept structurally separate, in `CapabilityDocs.evidence` rather than folded into `FieldDocs`, specifically so this different epistemic status is visible in the shape itself, not just in a doc comment (ADR 0053).

description.description: Why this field exists / what it's for.

owner.description: Overrides the capability's own `owner` for this field specifically.

sensitivity.description: Overrides the capability's own `sensitivity` for this field specifically.

protections.description: Overrides the capability's own `protections` for this field specifically.

retention.description: Documented retention policy for this field -- presence only, never an enforcement claim.

purpose.description: The declared reason this field's data is collected/retained. Declared only -- data-cap never verifies the stated purpose matches actual usage. Overrides the capability's own `purpose` for this field specifically.

legalBasis.description: The declared legal basis asserted for processing this field (e.g. `"consent"`, `"contract"`, `"legitimate interest"`). Records that a basis was declared -- never that data-cap has determined the basis is legally valid. Overrides the capability's own `legalBasis` for this field specifically.

dataResidency.description: The declared jurisdiction(s) this field's data is permitted/expected to be *stored* in -- a policy constraint, not an observed fact, not a processing-location claim, not a data-subject-location claim. Overrides the capability's own `dataResidency` for this field specifically.

auditRequired.description: Whether access to this field is documented as requiring an audit trail. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as `protections`/ `retention`. Overrides the capability's own `auditRequired` for this field specifically.

expiresAt.description: When this field's data (or the credential/source behind it) is declared to stop being valid, as an ISO-8601 date (`"2026-12-31"`). Declared only: nothing expires anything at runtime, and `data-cap` never fetches a real expiry from a provider. Build tooling reads it to report what is expiring soon (see the Lifecycle Model) -- a date that has already passed is reported as expired, never acted on.

deprecated.description: Whether this field is documented as deprecated. Presence-only, same discipline as every other declared fact here -- nothing warns at runtime.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this field is deprecated, and what to use instead. Only meaningful alongside `deprecated`.

removeBy.description: The date by which a deprecated field is intended to be removed, ISO-8601. Field-level only: a removal deadline is about one specific field's own migration, and a capability-wide `removeBy` would say nothing about which of its fields still need work.

renamedFrom.description: The previous name of this field, when it was renamed. Field-level only, for the same reason as `removeBy`. Build tooling uses this to correlate an added-field/removed-field pair across two runs into one rename rather than reporting an unrelated addition and deletion -- see `ChangeModel`'s `renamedFields`. Only ever populated from an *authored* value, never guessed from name similarity.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for -- opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package. Once a concept matters enough for data-cap to reason about, it gets its own named field above; everything else stays here.

FieldDocs.description:
Documentation metadata for one field.

`owner`, `sensitivity`, and `protections` override the capability-level value of the same name for this field specifically -- not every field in a capability is equally sensitive or equally owned. `protections` and `retention` are documentation-presence signals only: a generator may say a safeguard/policy is "documented" or "not documented," never that it is adequate, correct, or enforced. `purpose`/`legalBasis`/`dataResidency`/ `auditRequired` carry the same presence-only discipline -- declared governance facts, never a claim that data-cap has determined they satisfy any law (see `specs/decisions/0051-documentdata-metadata-and-governance-fields.md`).

The boundary this interface draws is deliberate: a named property here is reserved for a concept data-cap itself understands, projects, or reports on. Anything else -- organization-specific detail with no data-cap-defined meaning -- belongs in `metadata`, never as an ad hoc extra property, so this vocabulary stays bounded instead of accreting one-off keys over time.

Note what is deliberately absent: there is no per-field `validate`/ `validator` property, and no `helpers.validators` combinator library backing one, unlike `@maverickcer/env-cap`'s `EnvVarDocs`. That is a design choice, not a gap. `env-cap` validates on a reject-and-throw pipeline, where a failing validator must carry a message explaining the rejection; `data-cap` has no reject path to write a message for -- invalid processor/operation output resets the field to its declared default via `core/schema.ts`'s `checkValueAgainstSchema`, keeping fields synchronously readable (AGENTS.md invariant 2) and surfacing the mismatch through `DataInfo`. See `helpers/shape.ts`'s own module comment for the full reasoning.

source.description: Short identifier for where this operation acquires/sends data (e.g. `"stripe-api"`, `"postgres:users"`), not prose.

credentials.description: What's required to call this operation -- descriptive only, never an authorization/enforcement claim.

response.description: Documented shape of what this operation returns/produces.

endpoints.description: Declared data-flow boundaries this operation crosses -- see `DataFlowEndpoint`.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for -- opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package. The index signature below remains for the same reason it always has (documenting never fights the type checker); `metadata` is the recommended place for new extension data going forward.

OperationDocs.description:
Documentation metadata for one getter/mutator/subscription. Reserved keys are explicitly typed (mirroring the vocabulary real capabilities tend to document -- what it does, where it talks to, what it costs to call) while still accepting arbitrary extra keys for anything project-specific, so documenting never fights the type checker.

`credentials` is descriptive only -- documenting `credentials: "user session"` is never proof that authorization is actually enforced. `endpoints` is likewise author-declared, never verified.

direction.description: Which way data moves across this boundary.

kind.description: What kind of boundary this is.

name.description: Short identifier, e.g. "stripe-api", "postgres:users" -- a semantic label, not a sentence.

url.description: A literal, trackable location for this endpoint -- a URL, a route path, a `table:column` reference. Distinct from `name` (a short label): this is meant to be compared/matched across capabilities (e.g. flagging two capabilities that declare the same URL as likely-duplicate fetches), not just read by a person.

handling.description: The declared data-safety state of this field's value AT this specific boundary crossing -- e.g. a field that arrives `"encrypted"` on an `"input"` endpoint and is sent back out `"redacted"` on an `"output"` endpoint. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as every other field in this vocabulary: this records what a developer states about handling at this crossing, never that data-cap has verified the field's actual runtime value matches the claim.

DataFlowEndpoint.description: One declared data-flow boundary an operation crosses. A getter/ subscription's endpoints are typically `"input"` (where `execute`/ `subscribe` acquires data from); a mutator's are typically `"output"` (where it sends data to) -- nothing enforces the typical case, since this is documentation, not a runtime contract.

DataFlowDirection.description: Which direction data moves across a declared boundary, and what kind of boundary it is. Author-declared documentation only -- never statically verified against an operation's actual `execute`/`subscribe` body (those stay opaque per AGENTS.md invariant 6). A report may never present an endpoint as a proven fact; see AGENTS.md's declared-vs-proven invariant.

DataFlowEndpointKind.description: What kind of boundary a declared data-flow endpoint crosses -- a data store (`database`/`cache`/`storage`/`queue`), an external entity (`api`/`external-service`/`user-input`), or something internal to this codebase (`computed`/`internal`).

SourcePosition.description: A 1-based line/column within a file already known from context (e.g. `DependencyEdge.from`).

path.description: Top-level field key, as a single-element path (see the module doc comment on why granularity stops here).

docs.description: This field's own declared documentation, if any -- `description`/`protections`/`retention`/`metadata` have no resolution concept and live only here; for the six governed properties below, prefer `.value`/`.declaredOn` over reading this object directly (ADR 0057).

owner.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.owner`, else the capability's `owner`, plus which one declared it.

sensitivity.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.sensitivity`, else the capability's `sensitivity` -- same inheritance rule as `owner` (ADR 0049, ADR 0050, ADR 0057).

purpose.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.purpose`, else the capability's `purpose` -- same inheritance rule as `owner`/`sensitivity` (ADR 0051, ADR 0057). Declared only, never verified.

legalBasis.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.legalBasis`, else the capability's `legalBasis` -- same inheritance rule. A declared fact, never a legal determination (ADR 0051, ADR 0057).

dataResidency.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.dataResidency`, else the capability's `dataResidency` -- same inheritance rule. The declared permitted-storage jurisdiction(s), not an observed fact (ADR 0051, ADR 0057).

auditRequired.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.auditRequired`, else the capability's `auditRequired` -- same inheritance rule (ADR 0051, ADR 0057).

kind.description: Which kind of operation wrote this field.

writtenBy.description: Every getter/mutator/subscription whose statically-extracted `writes` shape claims this field.

shape.description: The field's literal-evaluated declared default -- structural comparison only (e.g. `structural-duplication.ts`), never a runtime value.

declarationPosition.description: Position of this field's own key in the `fields` object literal -- only when `fields` was resolved as an inline literal in this file; `undefined` when identifier-resolved across a file boundary this pass doesn't retain AST access to (never guessed at -- ADR 0052).

value.description: The effective value: the field's own declaration, else the capability's.

ResolvedGovernanceValue<string>.description: One resolved governance value plus its provenance (ADR 0057) -- the one path a `FieldNode` consumer reads for a governed property, replacing what used to require separately checking a bare resolved property AND `field.docs.X` to get the full picture. `declaredOn: undefined` means neither the field nor its capability declared a value at all (`value` is then also `undefined`).

value.description: The effective value: the field's own declaration, else the capability's.

ResolvedGovernanceValue<(string|string[].description: One resolved governance value plus its provenance (ADR 0057) -- the one path a `FieldNode` consumer reads for a governed property, replacing what used to require separately checking a bare resolved property AND `field.docs.X` to get the full picture. `declaredOn: undefined` means neither the field nor its capability declared a value at all (`value` is then also `undefined`).

value.description: The effective value: the field's own declaration, else the capability's.

ResolvedGovernanceValue<boolean>.description: One resolved governance value plus its provenance (ADR 0057) -- the one path a `FieldNode` consumer reads for a governed property, replacing what used to require separately checking a bare resolved property AND `field.docs.X` to get the full picture. `declaredOn: undefined` means neither the field nor its capability declared a value at all (`value` is then also `undefined`).

kind.description: Which kind of operation this is.

docs.description: This operation's own declared documentation, if any.

writes.description: Top-level field paths this operation's statically-extracted `writes` shape covers. Empty when `writes` was absent (on a getter/subscription) or unresolvable -- never guessed at.

hasProcessor.description: Whether this operation's config object literal declares a `processor` key -- a proven, structural presence fact (never an evaluation of what the processor does; see ADR 0050).

hasOptimistic.description: Whether this operation's config object literal declares an `optimistic` key -- structurally always `false` for a getter/subscription.

endpoints.description: Hoisted from `docs.endpoints` for convenient lookup -- author-declared, never statically verified.

OperationNode.description: One getter/mutator/subscription operation, resolved from the inventory's shared model.

file.description: Absolute path (or synthetic label, e.g. `"(package) name"`) the warning applies to.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what was skipped and why.

ParseWarning.description: A recoverable issue found while statically parsing or linking one capability file -- never fatal, always surfaced to the caller as data.

capabilities.description: Only capabilities with at least one lifecycle-relevant field set, at the capability level or on at least one field. Sorted by `file` then `exportName`.

expiring.description: Every capability-/field-level `expiresAt` within the configured window, soonest-first (already-expired entries sort first, since their `daysRemaining` is negative).

LifecycleModel.description: `data-cap`'s Lifecycle Model: declared expiry/deprecation/rename data, plus the expiring-soon view.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path -- carried through verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file`.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

expiresAt.description: Declared ISO-8601 expiry for the capability as a whole.

deprecated.description: Whether the capability is documented as deprecated.

retention.description: Declared retention policy at the capability level.

fields.description: Only fields with at least one lifecycle field set, sorted by path -- same "only what's relevant" scope the rendered report uses.

LifecycleModelCapability.description: One capability's declared lifecycle data, plus every lifecycle-bearing field under it.

path.description: The field's path within its capability -- `readonly string[]`, matching every other model's field addressing (never a flat key string).

expiresAt.description: Declared ISO-8601 expiry, unparsed and uninterpreted here.

deprecated.description: Whether the field is documented as deprecated.

removeBy.description: Declared ISO-8601 removal deadline -- field-level only (see `core/document.ts`).

renamedFrom.description: The field's previous name, when authored -- what `ChangeModel.renamedFields` correlates against.

retention.description: Declared retention policy -- a policy statement, deliberately independent of `expiresAt`'s temporal constraint (a field can be retained long after its source credential expires, and vice versa).

LifecycleModelField.description: One field's declared lifecycle data. Only fields with at least one of these set appear in the model at all.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the declaring file.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

field.description: `undefined` for a capability-level `expiresAt`, set for a per-field one.

expiresAt.description: The raw ISO-8601 date string, exactly as declared.

daysRemaining.description: Whole days from `now` until expiry; negative when already expired.

ExpiringEntry.description: One capability- or field-level `expiresAt` falling within the configured window (or already past it).

dependency.description: Whether a usage scan ran and produced a Dependency Model this run.

ownership.description: Whether an Ownership Model was built this run.

finding.description: Whether at least one rule/scan pass ran and produced a Finding Model this run.

change.description: Whether a manifest diff was available and produced a Change Model this run.

EvidenceComputedModels.description:
Which project-varying sub-models this particular run actually computed (OUT-04).

Without this, a persisted `data.evidence.json` is ambiguous in exactly the way a governance artifact must never be: an absent `dependency` could mean "nothing in this project depends on anything" (a real, reportable finding) or "this run never scanned for dependencies" (no finding at all, just an un-run pass). Those are opposite conclusions and the JSON looked identical either way.

env-cap solves the same ambiguity by always computing all six sub-models, so absence never happens. `data-cap` deliberately does not follow that: the usage scan is the expensive pass here, and `--docs` alone is supposed to stay cheap. So instead of forcing every run to pay for a full dependency scan, each sub-model's presence is stated explicitly.

`capability`, `lifecycle`, and `runtimeContract` have no flag -- they are always populated by construction, so a flag could only ever read `true`.

A pass that ran and found nothing is `true` with an empty result, never `false`: "we looked and found none" is a genuine finding, and collapsing it into "we didn't look" is precisely the confusion this field exists to prevent.

edges.description: Every proven edge, unindexed -- same array `scanDependencies` produced.

DependencyModel.description: `data-cap`'s Dependency Model: every proven `DependencyEdge`, unindexed. See `dependency-projections.ts` for on-demand capability/consumer groupings.

relationship.description: Which kind of connection this is -- see `DependencyRelationship`.

from.description: The consuming file, as a root-relative POSIX path (OUT-01, see `display-path.ts`).

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring the capability -- the same value `CapabilityNode.file` publishes.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

field.description: The specific field path being read, when `relationship` is `"reads-field"`.

operation.description: The specific operation name being called, when `relationship` is `"calls-getter"`/`"calls-mutator"`/`"calls-subscription"`.

resolution.description: Whether the consumer reference itself was unambiguously resolved -- see the usage-scan pass for what each value means.

position.description: Position of the access site in `from` (file already known via `from`), when this edge originates from a specific identifier reference (every relationship except the file-level `"imports"` fallback edge scan-dependencies.ts synthesizes for a consumer with no further resolved usage).

DependencyEdge.description: A statically-proven connection from one consuming file to a capability (or a specific field/operation on it). Unlike the declared metadata in `core/document.ts` (`source`, `credentials`, `endpoints`), every `DependencyEdge` is derived by AST analysis, never author-declared -- see AGENTS.md's declared-vs-proven invariant. Produced by the usage-scan pass (`scan-dependencies.ts`), not by this module.

OwnershipModel.description: `data-cap`'s Ownership Model: the owner -> {capabilities, fields} matrix, versioned for JSON publication.

capabilities.description: Capabilities this owner is accountable for at the capability level.

fields.description: Individual fields (on capabilities not wholly owned by this owner) they're accountable for.

OwnershipMatrixEntry.description: One owner's row in the ownership matrix -- every capability and field they're accountable for.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring this capability -- carried through verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file` (see `display-path.ts`).

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

OwnershipCapabilityRef.description: Identifies one capability by where it's declared.

capability.description: The capability that owns this field.

field.description: The field's path within its capability.

OwnershipFieldRef.description: Identifies one field, owned by a specific capability.

findings.description: Every finding, each with its `location` computed.

FindingModel.description: `data-cap`'s Finding Model: every finding, with a structured, pre-computed `location`.

code.description: Which kind of fact this finding reports.

family.description: Which analysis pass produced this finding -- see `ReportFindingFamily`.

severity.description: How strongly this finding should be treated.

LocatedFinding.description: One finding, with its structured `location` computed -- and *only* that (OUT-02). A rule/scan emits a `ReportFinding` carrying the raw, optional `capability`/`field`/`operation`/`source`/`position`/`indeterminateSites` locators (see `findings.ts`); `locationOf` resolves all six into one required, structured `location`, and this type then drops them, so a consumer has exactly one path to "where does this point" instead of a structured answer sitting next to six flat ones that say the same thing (and could drift apart under a hand-constructed value). Two names for one lineage: emit a `ReportFinding`, consume a `LocatedFinding`.

indeterminateSites.description: Every candidate access site a `"FIELD_ACCESS_INDETERMINATE"` finding could actually be about (ADR 0052) -- populated only for that code. Lives here, on the one variant that can carry it, rather than as a flat sibling of `location`: a field-level finding is the only kind that ever has one. Spans potentially multiple consuming files, so each entry carries its own `file` (`SourceLocation`, not just `SourcePosition`).

FindingLocation.description: Where a finding points, as a discriminated union -- never a formatted string a consumer would have to parse back apart. Ships with only the variants `findings.ts`'s actual emission sites produce today (`"capability"`/`"field"`/`"consumer"`/`"none"`); `"operation"` is included because `ReportFinding.operation` is already part of that type's public shape, even though no current finding populates it -- trivially reachable the day one does, not a guess about what it would look like. `"capability"`/`"field"`/`"operation"` carry an optional `position` (ADR 0052) -- the declaration site's own position, when the source `ReportFinding.position` was populated; `"consumer"` doesn't, since it locates a *consuming file*, which has no single declaration position the way a capability/field/operation's own declaration does.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring the capability -- carried through verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file` (see `display-path.ts`).

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

FindingLocationCapability.description: A finding's capability locator -- shared by every `FindingLocation` variant except `"none"`.

SourceLocation.description: A `SourcePosition` plus the file it's in, for anywhere the file isn't already implied by the surrounding structure (e.g. a finding's list of candidate sites spanning multiple files).

ReportFindingCode.description: Every kind of fact a static rule or usage-scan/data-flow pass can report.

ReportFindingFamily.description:
Which analysis pass a finding came out of -- an orthogonal axis to `severity` (how much it matters) and `code` (exactly what it is).

This is what makes the `--strict*` flags' own groupings legible in the output rather than only in the orchestrator's source: `--strict-docs` escalates `"governance"`/`"structural"`/`"citation"`, `--strict-ownership` escalates `"usage"`, `--strict-flow` escalates `"flow"`. A consumer filtering a report ("show me only what a usage scan proved") currently has to hardcode a list of `ReportFindingCode`s and keep it in sync by hand; `family` makes that a real, stable field instead.

Deliberately assigned at the emission site, never derived from `code` by a lookup table: the rule that produces a finding is the only thing that actually knows which pass it belongs to, and a table would be a second source of truth to drift out of sync (the same reasoning that keeps `severity` at the emission site).

ReportSeverity.description: How strongly a finding should be treated: `info` never blocks, `warning` blocks only under `--strict*`, `error` always blocks.

blastRadius.description: One entry per added/updated capability, or `undefined` when no `DependencyModel` was supplied -- an optional layer, matching `--ownership`/`--flow`'s existing opt-in cost model (the usage scan isn't free).

renamedFields.description: Every added-field/removed-field pair this run's currently-declared `renamedFrom` values correlate into a single rename, sorted by capability key then current name.

ChangeModel.description: `data-cap`'s Change Model: the manifest diff, plus an optional blast-radius index.

addedCapabilities.description: Capability keys present in the new snapshot but not the previous one.

removedCapabilities.description: Capability keys present in the previous snapshot but not the new one.

updatedCapabilities.description: Capability keys present in both snapshots whose shape changed.

ManifestChangeReport.description: The diff between two `ManifestSnapshot`s, in a fixed Added/Removed/Updated shape.

changes.description: Human-readable description of each individual change (e.g. `"owner changed from... to..."`).

fields.description: The same field-level diff `changes` describes in prose, as data (EVD-05). Added so `ChangeModel`'s rename correlation has something to match against without re-parsing a human-readable sentence -- a report deriving structure back out of its own prose is exactly the kind of fragility this codebase avoids. `changes` is unaffected and still reads the same.

ManifestCapabilityUpdate.description: One capability whose snapshot shape changed between two runs.

added.description: Field names present now but not in the previous snapshot, sorted.

removed.description: Field names present in the previous snapshot but not now, sorted.

ManifestFieldDiff.description: The structured added/removed field-name diff for one changed capability.

capability.description: The capability key (`file#exportName`) -- matches `ManifestChangeReport`'s own key convention.

consumers.description: Distinct consuming files known (from Dependency Model) to depend on this capability right now, sorted.

BlastRadiusEntry.description: One changed capability's known current consumers.

capability.description: The owning capability's key (`file#exportName`) -- a rename never crosses capabilities.

previousName.description: The field's name before the rename -- matches a `removed` entry in that capability's own field diff.

currentName.description: The field's name after the rename -- matches an `added` entry in the same diff.

RenamedField.description: One added-field/removed-field pair correlated into a single rename via the current declaration's `renamedFrom` (EVD-05).

packageVersion.description: The `data-cap` package version this model describes -- read from `package.json`, the same way `cli/json.ts`'s `TOOL_VERSION` is.

RuntimeContractModel.description: `data-cap`'s Runtime Contract Model: the package's own documented execution guarantees.

key.description: A short, stable identifier for this fact (e.g. `"getter-concurrency"`).

governingAdr.description: The ADR number (e.g. `"0024"`) that governs this fact -- always a real file under `specs/decisions/`.

module.description: The source file that implements this guarantee, root-relative.

RuntimePolicyFact.description: One documented runtime guarantee, traced to the ADR that governs it.
